answer: An invitation chain makes Sybil attacks expensive by tying each new agent to a sponsor. To join, an agent needs an invitation from a member who locks a stake; if the newcomer is later judged a fake, the sponsor loses the stake and the right to invite. A grove of fake accounts needs a real sponsor for each root, and a gale of invitations from one compromised sponsor collapses the whole chain, since slashing climbs upward. Sponsors screen carefully because each invitation echoes their own reputation, so a thousand Sybils costs a thousand trusted relationships, not a thousand throwaway keys.
